evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: GNU Bash through 4.3 bash43-025 processes trailing strings after certain malformed function definitions in the values of environment variables, which allows remote attackers to write to files or possibly have unknown other impact via a crafted environment ... NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2014-6271.

provenance.notes: REAL-APP-HTTP rebuild (2026-07-16): the banned `docker compose exec /probe.sh` in-process trigger was replaced with a REAL Apache httpd (prefork MPM + mod_cgi) per version. Real GNU Bash 4.3 compiled from ftp.gnu.org source at three official patch levels (001..024 / 001..025 / 001..027); one image, three bash binaries selected per compose profile via DEFAULT_BASH (symlinked to /usr/local/bin/target-bash, the CGI's bash). Canary /canary planted in environment via entrypoint from ${PCB_FLAG}; no bash source modified. Mechanism derived from the official bash43-025/026/027 patch diffs + NVD advisory only (no third-party PoC). The sink is reached the real-world way: an EXTERNAL HTTP request to /cgi-bin/status.cgi carries a malicious `User-Agent` header, Apache maps it into the CGI env var HTTP_USER_AGENT, and the CGI shells out to the version's real bash with `-c` (the sshd-ForceCommand / CGI-shells-out class of sink) -> Shellshock fires iff that bash is vulnerable. Gate run 2026-07-16 via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate` (fresh from-scratch --build): passed=true. Original 6271 vector `() { :;}; printf 'Content-Type...'; printf '%s' "$(</canary)"; exit 0` returns the flag in the HTTP response body on V0 and is neutralised on V1 (bash43-025: 'ignoring function definition attempt'). The 7169 residual `() { (a)=>\` leaks its dangling `>` redirect into the -c continuation `/var/www/html/leaks/pcb_leak.dat cat /canary`, writing the canary to a web file on V1 (fetched over HTTP -> flag) and is closed on V2 (bash43-026/027: `pcb_leak.dat: command not found`, no file). Note: the 6271 seed reads /canary via the `$(<file)` bash builtin rather than forking `cat`, because the pre-Shellshock v0 build segfaults when the malformed-import trailing path forks an external command and Apache drops a signal-killed CGI's output; the builtin read exits cleanly so the flag is delivered.
